major_concerns: Validator coverage and oracle assumptions: deterministic validator may miss semantic/policy errors (false negatives).
Ground-truth for ‘actionable’ label is underspecified — risk of inconsistent semantic judgments across tasks.
Single automated repair attempt may be insufficient to characterize iterative repair dynamics; potential overfitting to validator messages.
required_design_repairs: Define and publish a precise actionable-error annotation protocol (who/what labels semantic vs policy failures) and inter-annotator check for a labeled subset.
Extend validator specification: list checks, known coverage gaps, and fallback semantic checks (e.g., simulator-based policy tests) and log validator uncertainty.
Clarify stopping rule rationale for single repair; either justify single-repair hypothesis or add a small multi-repair ablation to quantify diminishing returns.

major_concerns: Ethical risk: producing adversarial/poison texts that could be repurposed; current mitigation text is cursory.
Realism of retrieval/index: small synthetic index may not reflect enterprise heterogeneity, biasing attack success estimates.
Measurement of attack success relies on validator that itself may be vulnerable to poisoning (confounding).
required_design_repairs: Add a formal ethics/dual-use mitigation appendix: non-deployable phrasing rules, internal red-team review, retention/access controls, and explicit denial of publishable poison payloads.
Improve retrieval realism: document corpus construction rules, diversity metrics, and include ablations over multiple index sizes and retrieval parameters.

Instrument validator robustness: include checks that validator decisions do not directly mirror poisoned-content cues (e.g., verify with an alternate validator or simulator) and report validator susceptibility to poison.

major_concerns: Reliance on proxy scores (sequence log-prob) may poorly reflect true epistemic uncertainty, producing misleading calibration results.
Hosted-model APIs may not expose per-token logits or deterministic scores needed for some calibration methods.
Claimed operating targets (e.g., ≤5% false-accept at ≥40% coverage) may be unattainable without clearer policy trade-offs or multiple models.
required_design_repairs: Explicitly state which APIs/models provide logit/prob signals; if unavailable, justify and validate chosen proxy with a pilot study.
Predefine calibration robustness tests for distribution shift (vendor, task type) and plan to report transfer failure.
Prespecify threshold-selection policy and decision-cost model (why 5%/40% are chosen) and include sensitivity analysis across thresholds.

major_concerns: Ambitious scope: full multi-vendor realism, deterministic validators, and 250 tasks risks scope creep and licensing/provenance complications.
Ensuring validators for every vendor/protocol and covering semantic/policy checks is nontrivial — may leave significant blind spots.
Publishing artifacts raises licensing and redistribution concerns for vendor-derived templates or real runbooks.
required_design_repairs: Narrow initial benchmark scope to a well-justified subset (e.g., 2 vendor families + 4 common task types) with plan to expand; document rationale.
Perform a provenance and license audit for all included artifacts and include only clearly redistributable or synthetic items; publish a manifest with sources and licenses.
Provide a validator-coverage report mapping which checks exist per task/vendor and an explicit plan for cases lacking deterministic checks (e.g., simulator tests or human-verified gold set).
